title: On-device constraint-aware tokenizer probe
content:
Purpose / problem statement:

This is a personal probe into a compact, constraint-aware tokenizer and preprocessor intended for on-device LLM clients (mobile/web-worker/edge). The constraint set is: limited memory (~20–200MB working), tight latency budgets (<=30ms pre-tokenize), and token-budget-aware chunking for streaming requests where we want graceful degradation when budgets are exceeded.

Objectives (what I want this to achieve):
- Single small library that runs in JS (wasm) and native (C++) with identical heuristics and deterministic behaviour.
- Exposes an API that supports: cheap peek-without-alloc, partial-tokenization for streaming input, budget-aware chunking, and a compact trace for telemetry.
- Plays nicely with on-device prefix caching and KV-cache eviction heuristics.
- Deterministic fallback path when device runs out of memory or time (e.g., offload tokenization to server or use approximate token counts).

High-level design ideas (brain dump):
1) Two-phase tokenizer pipeline:
   - fast-pass: byte-level rough-scan that identifies whitespace boundaries, punctuation runs, and candidate split anchors. Very cheap; returns a lightweight index of spans (start,len,type).
   - exact-pass: full subword/gpt-bpe/vocab lookup only for spans that will actually be emitted now (or for a small horizon).
   Rationale: most user inputs are short or have obvious anchors; avoid expensive lookup for everything.

2) Budget-aware chunker
   - API accepts token_budget_hint (int) and max_latency_ms (int).
   - Token_budget_hint is a soft cap; chunker produces chunks whose estimated token_len <= budget, prioritized by semantic boundaries (sentences, punctuation).
   - Estimation uses a lightweight model: avg_subtokens_per_utf8_char per locale + punctuation multiplier + numeric heuristics. Fall back to deterministic token_count() when budget is generous.

3) Peek and commit flow (stream-friendly)
   - peek(n_bytes) -> returns rough spans and estimated tokens for first n_bytes with no heap allocations beyond a pre-allocated ring buffer.
   - commit(n_bytes) -> mark bytes consumed for next peek. Useful when client receives incremental keystrokes or websockets streaming partial edits.

4) Memory-safety and graceful fallback
   - Library keeps an upper working-set threshold (configurable). When near threshold, switch to approximate-mode: use char-based estimates and avoid exact-pass; return a flag 'approximate:true'.
   - If memory request fails or exact-pass times out, return a fallback tokenization digest: {approx_tokens, anchor_spans} and a minimal context hash to allow server-side re-join.

5) Telemetry / tracing (compact)
   - We need a tiny trace string per request for debugging: format "v1|p=12|e=84|m=0|f=1" (peek_count, estimated_tokens, mode, fallback) to avoid heavy payloads.
   - Optionally include sample of token ids for first N tokens (N small) when in dev mode.

API shape (sketch, JS-like):

// init with compiled vocab + config
Tok = TokLib.init({vocabUrl, maxWorkingMB: 48, locale: 'en-us', mode: 'auto'});
// streaming usage
Tok.peek(bytesAvailable, {maxLatencyMs: 20, tokenBudgetHint: 60}) -> {
  anchors: [ {start: 0, len: 34, type: 'sentence'}, ... ],
  est_tokens: 18,
  mode: 'approx'|'exact',
  trace: 'v1|p=2|e=18|m=1|f=0'
}
Tok.commit(consumedBytes);
Tok.tokenizeSpan(span, {forceExact: false}) -> {tokens: [ '▁The', 're', '##sult' ], token_ids: [123,45,6], exact: true}
Tok.estimateTokensForUtf8Slice(buf, start, len) -> 9 // constant-time-ish estimate
Tok.offloadDigest() -> base64-digest (used to rehydrate on server)

Configuration knobs (user-level):
- mode: 'exact'|'approx'|'auto'
- maxWorkingMB: integer
- token_budget_policy: 'strict'|'prefer_semantic'|'allow_overrun'
- localeHints: ['en','zh'] to inform avg subtoken tables

Edge-cases / unresolved questions:
- How to handle edits (backspace mid-chunk) while server already started generation? Need stable anchors with rebase. Maybe commit() returns a rebase token that the server can use to reconcile edits.
- Do we keep the whole vocab in wasm? That defeats memory goals. Alternative: compact bloom-ish membership + server fallback for OOVs. But bloom false-positives could flip token counts. Need experiments.
- Non-determinism across platforms (wasm vs native) is a risk; we need canonical seeded hash for unknown tokenization ties.
- CJK languages: whitespace heuristics don't apply; must rely on different anchors (punctuation + character n-gram heuristics).

Approx-mode heuristics (notes):
- base = ceil(len_utf8 * avg_subtokens_per_char[locale])
- add +1 for punctuation-run >3 chars, +2 for long numeric blocks (>9 digits), +ceil(non-ASCII_ratio*2)
- clip to max of physical_words*3 to avoid blowups

Telemetry experiments to run (quick experiments list):
- compare exact tokens vs approx estimate error distribution on internal S sample (10k user utterances) across locales
- memory footprint of wasm with and without full vocab; trade-off lines
- latency of peek(256) on mid-range Android and on iPhone SE equivalent

Implementation plan (rough):
- P0: implement two-phase tokenizer with small english-only avg table + JS wasm prototype; basic peek/commit API (3 weeks)
- P1: add locale tables, approx-mode heuristics, compact trace format (2 weeks)
- P2: integrate offloadDigest/rehydration protocol with server-side rejoin (depends on backend ticket ENGINF-3421) (3 weeks)
- P3: run telemetry collection in opt-in dev channel, compare accuracy & adjust heuristics (2 weeks)

Sidenotes / random thoughts:
- Might be useful to expose a tiny interactive web playground (single-page) that shows peek/commit windows and how chunks map to model tokens; super helpful for SDK docs.
- Could sync with client-side prefix-cache eviction: token_estimates can be used to decide which prefix to keep in persistent store.
- We should add scam-detection heuristics: huge numeric blobs or base64 payloads should be flagged and compressed/replaced with a single sentinel token estimate.

TODOs (what I need to do next):
- write minimal wasm prototype: linear buffer scanning + small token table (Use existing BPE implementation as reference but cap memory) -- assign to me
- create ENGINF ticket linking offload rehydrate protocol (server join) -- dependent on backend
- run small measurement on 5k utterances to calibrate avg_subtokens_per_char table and seed approximator
- discuss with Priya about canonicalization behaviour across platforms (determinism)

Notes to self: keep the API surface minimal. Users will be happiest if peek/commit + tokeniseSpan + estimateTokens are available; everything else can be opt-in advanced config.

References / links in brain:
- previous tokenization lab notes (see linked artifacts)
- small paper: "Approximate Token Counts for Budgeted Text Generation" (internal abstract idea)

End of probe notes.

-- maya
